trust_decision.summary: Paths from .skills.toml (destination, source_path), CLI/prompt targets and fork names, plus symlinks inside library/project skill folders, are untrusted; the decision is whether each joined path stays lexically under the project or library root and whether copy/replace may follow a symlink. Before the fix only detect --target checked is_absolute; the fix adds a component check at config load, at every push/pull join, in detect, in fork-name validation, and symlink refusal in fs_util.

landing_point.why: Summary says traversal/symlink-follow allows deletion; the obvious sink is cwd.join(installed.destination) handed to replace_folder_contents -> remove_dir_all in pull (src/fs_util.rs:24-26).

fix_sites.entry_point: skillctl add / detect / pull (fork-locally) via copy_dir_all; push/pull via replace_folder_contents
every command that loads .skills.toml (add, pull, push, detect, diff/classify)
skillctl detect interactive custom path prompt

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/project_config.rs:34 (toml::from_str of .skills.toml with no validation; fix adds InstalledSkill::validate at load, fix.diff:900-930)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The loader is 'just deserialization' and the sinks are in push/pull; a solver guarding only the push/pull joins (or only remove_dir_all) leaves load() accepting absolute/.. entries, which hidden tests on load() or on other consumers (diff/classify, read_tags) would catch. For O8: --dest is the operator's own flag, and parent-directory symlinks are declared out of the threat model by the fix itself.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: detect --target '.' / empty path must keep meaning library root, dotted paths like .claude/skills/foo must be accepted, and destinations that do not yet exist must still be installable; a canonicalize-based or 'no leading dot' check breaks these, and rejecting all symlinks anywhere (including the operator's own cwd/library cache parents) would over-harden.

O6_input_shapes: '..' at start, middle and end of path
symlink to file inside skill folder
symlink to directory inside skill folder
interactive prompt input as well as CLI flag

O8_uncovered_routes.route: skillctl add --dest (and interactive custom path) is joined with the library folder name and remove_dir_all'd on --on-conflict overwrite with no relative-subpath check, although the CLI documents it as relative to the project root.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: --dest is typed by the operator, not read from attacker-controlled .skills.toml or library content.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different file from landing point (src/commands/add.rs vs src/commands/pull.rs); doc at src/cli.rs:83

O8_uncovered_routes.route: add's overwrite path deletes with fs::remove_dir_all directly instead of replace_folder_contents, so the new symlinked-destination refusal does not cover it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: std remove_dir_all does not follow a top-level symlink, and the advisory names pull/push/detect as the deletion routes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file from landing point and from fs_util.rs

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A symlinked intermediate directory (e.g. a project-committed .claude or a library 'skills' dir linked elsewhere) passes the lexical check, so replace_folder_contents still deletes outside the root.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix explicitly declares parent symlinks out of the threat model (fix.diff:768-772) and avoids canonicalize for TOCTOU reasons.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same sink as landing point; also src/commands/push.rs:320-333

O8b_injection_room.sibling: classify joins installed.destination without safe_join; a 'repair/clean' step here that deletes a stale local_dir would be a realistic second delete route
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: classify already resolves local_dir for every installed skill; a maintainer adding cleanup of LocalMissing/LibraryMissing would reuse it (upstream later added a remove command, latest/src/commands/remove.rs:222-230).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: read_tags on cwd.join(destination)/SKILL.md could become a content-reading path (e.g. printing description) reached before any sink-side check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Tag/description display is a natural feature; it relies only on load-time validation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: fork_op_for_name builds new_library_path from source_path.parent(); a variant taking a user-supplied library subdir (like detect --target) without the shared validator
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: detect already has such a target option; mirroring it for push --fork is plausible.

O9_family: path traversal / symlink following (CWE-22, CWE-61) leading to arbitrary file read-back and directory deletion
